title: Pulse_Secure_VPN_Compromise_Investigation_6b8
description: Your organization has detected unusual activity on its Pulse Secure VPN appliances. Initial analysis suggests a potential compromise by the RADIALPULSE backdoor malware. Your task is to investigate the compromised hosts, identify the malware's behavior, and contain the threat.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: Your organization has detected unusual activity on its Pulse Secure VPN appliances. Initial analysis suggests a potential compromise by the RADIALPULSE backdoor malware. Your task is to investigate the compromised hosts, identify the malware's behavior, and contain the threat. You will need to identify specific services, timers, and network ports as part of your investigation.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the target host via SSH using the following credentials: Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano.
levels.local_content: Access the target host via SSH using the following credentials: Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano.

levels.title: Suspicious Service Discovery
levels.content: While monitoring the network, you noticed unusual outbound connections from the target host. Investigate the target host to identify any unauthorized or suspicious services running.
levels.solution: To identify suspicious services, you can use commands like `systemctl list-units --type=service` or `ps aux` to list all running services and processes. Look for any services that seem out of place or unfamiliar. The flag you are looking for is `payload-transfer.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the list of running services and look for any that seem out of place or unfamiliar.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use commands like `systemctl list-units --type=service` or `ps aux` to list all running services and processes.

levels.title: Persistence Discovery
levels.content: You have identified a suspicious service running on the target host. Determine how this service is automatically started after a system reboot.
levels.solution: To identify persistence mechanisms, examine systemd services and timers using commands like `systemctl list-unit-files --type=service` and `systemctl list-timers`. Look for any services or timers related to the suspicious service. The flag you are looking for is `payload-transfer.timer`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Examine systemd services and timers to find any related to the suspicious service.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use commands like `systemctl list-unit-files --type=service` and `systemctl list-timers` to identify persistence mechanisms.

levels.title: C2 Communication Discovery (Port)
levels.content: The suspicious service appears to be communicating with an external command-and-control (C2) server. Determine which network port is used for this communication.
levels.solution: To identify the network port used for C2 communication, use commands like `ss -tulnp` or `netstat -tulnp` to list all network connections and listening ports. Look for any connections or ports related to the suspicious service. The flag you are looking for is `4444`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the network connections and listen ports to find the one used by the suspicious service.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use commands like `ss -tulnp` or `netstat -tulnp` to list all network connections and listening ports.
